commands.review_summary:
The PR changes `resolveApiKeyForProvider` so incompatible unlocked profiles fall through to normal auth resolution, and adds resolver tests for fallback versus locked-profile fail-fast behavior.

PR surface: Source +16, Tests +81. Total +97 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. at source level. Current main asserts on an inherited OpenAI OAuth profile before auth.order fallback, and the PR-introduced regression is visible because `/btw` forwards a user-sourced profile without `lockedProfile`.
commands.review_followup: - [P2] A narrow automated repair is feasible because the blocker is mechanical: make fallback explicit and compaction-only instead of global for unlocked profileId calls.

target.title: fix(slack): validate redirect targets against Slack hostname allowlist (SSRF)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`fetchWithSlackAuth` in `extensions/slack/src/monitor/media.ts` validated the initial URL via `assertSlackFileUrl` (Slack hostname check), but then handed redirect handling to fetch's `redirect: "follow"` — which follows up to 20 hops to **any HTTPS URL** without re-checking the hostname. A redirect from a Slack host to an arbitrary endpoint (internal service, attacker host, cloud metadata) bypassed the SSRF guard entirely.

## Why This Change Was Made

The old code only checked `resolvedUrl.protocol === "https:"` after the first redirect, then let `redirect: "follow"` take over. The sibling `createSlackMediaFetch` (same file) and the canonical `src/infra/net/fetch-guard.ts` both use `redirect: "manual"` with hostname validation. `fetchWithSlackAuth` was the inconsistent outlier.

The function has no prod caller today (prod Slack media uses `saveRemoteMedia` → canonical fetch-guard), but it is an exported public API. Fixing the SSRF shape now prevents a future caller from inheriting the bypass.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior change (no prod caller). The exported `fetchWithSlackAuth` now safely bounds redirects to Slack hostnames, blocking SSRF via redirect if any future caller adopts it.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed:** `fetchWithSlackAuth` followed redirects to arbitrary HTTPS URLs (bypassing the Slack hostname check), enabling SSRF if the function were called from a message-handling path.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux x86_64, Node v24.14.0, commit `38b218204a` on branch `fix/slack-fetch-auth-ssrf-redirect-guard`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx verify-slack-ssrf-real.mjs` — stands up a **real local HTTPS server** (self-signed cert) that emits real `302` redirects, points the production undici dispatcher at a custom DNS lookup (`127.0.0.1` for every host, `rejectUnauthorized: false`), and calls the real exported `fetchWithSlackAuth`. `globalThis.fetch` is **not** replaced, so the production `fetchWithRuntimeDispatcher` (undici) path handles every hop over a real socket. The server logs each request it actually receives (host + whether the `Authorization` header was sent), proving exactly where the guard intervenes.
- **Evidence after fix:** Terminal capture of `node` runtime verification (live stdout, copied verbatim — non-mocked, real sockets):

  ```text
  $ node --import tsx verify-slack-ssrf-real.mjs
  real local HTTPS server (self-signed); undici Agent DNS overridden to 127.0.0.1
  globalThis.fetch is NOT replaced — production undici runtime fetch is exercised

  [Case 1] real GET https://files.slack.com:47823/ok
    [server recv] host=files.slack.com  path=/ok  authorization=present
    -> status=200  content-type=image/jpeg

  [Case 3] real GET https://files.slack.com:47823/to-internal  (302 -> non-Slack host)
    [server recv] host=files.slack.com  path=/to-internal  authorization=present
    threw Error: Refusing Slack media redirect to non-Slack host "internal.corp.example.com"
    => guard refused the non-Slack redirect target before any second network hop

  [Case 4] real GET https://files.slack.com:47823/to-cdn  (302 -> cdn.slack-edge.com)
    [server recv] host=files.slack.com  path=/to-cdn  authorization=present
    [server recv] host=cdn.slack-edge.com  path=/file  authorization=(none)
    -> status=200

  Verdict: real-network SSRF guard verified
  ```

- **Observed result after fix:** Against real sockets (no mocked fetch), a Slack URL that returns `302` to `internal.corp.example.com` throws `Refusing Slack media redirect to non-Slack host "internal.corp.example.com"` and the server logs **only** the first hop — no second connection is ever made to the internal host (the guard refuses the redirect target before fetching it). A cross-origin Slack redirect (`files.slack.com` → `cdn.slack-edge.com`) is followed to completion (status 200) and the server logs the second hop with `authorization=(none)`, confirming the `Authorization` header is stripped on the cross-origin hop. Legitimate non-redirect Slack GETs return 200 unchanged.
- **What was not tested:** A live redirect served by the real `api.slack.com` / `files.slack.com` edge (the function has no production caller; the local HTTPS server with an undici DNS override is the closest non-mocked reproduction of the network redirect path).

## Tests and validation

```text
$ pnpm test extensions/slack/src/monitor/media.test.ts
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)

$ pnpm tsgo:extensions:test
EXIT=0 (type check passed)
```

Added two SSRF regression tests: redirect to a non-Slack host throws, redirect to non-HTTPS throws. Updated existing redirect tests to expect `redirect: "manual"` on the second hop (the loop no longer hands off to `redirect: "follow"`).

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior: No - the function has no prod caller; prod Slack media uses `saveRemoteMedia` with the canonical fetch-guard.
- Config/env/migration behavior: No - no config or env surface touched.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool execution: Yes (improvement) - closes an SSRF bypass where redirects could reach arbitrary HTTPS hosts; every redirect hop is now re-validated against the Slack hostname allowlist and cross-origin hops strip Authorization.
- Plugins/providers/channels/SDK: No - internal helper in the Slack plugin; the function signature is unchanged.
- Highest-risk area: a future caller that relied on the old redirect-follow-to-anywhere behavior would break — but no such caller exists today, and the old behavior was a security bug.
- Mitigation: 45 media tests (incl. two new SSRF regression cases) + non-mocked node runtime verification over real sockets + tsgo green.

Closes: N/A (no existing issue)
